extracted.intended_audience: dataset creators and dataset consumers in machine learning (researchers, practitioners, product teams, policy makers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a question-driven workflow for creating 'datasheets for datasets' that document a dataset's motivation, composition, collection, preprocessing, uses, distribution, and maintenance to increase transparency and inform dataset consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document dataset motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: For what purpose was the dataset created? Was there a specific task in mind? Was there a specific gap that needed to be filled? Please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to encourage dataset creators to clearly articulate reasons for creating the dataset and to promote transparency about funding interests; useful for dataset consumers to understand intended uses and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify dataset creators
rubrics_metrics.description: Who created the dataset (e.g., which team, research group) and on behalf of which entity (e.g., company, institution, organization)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps consumers attribute provenance and contact appropriate parties; relevant for accountability and follow-up questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document dataset funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Who funded the creation of the dataset? If there is an associated grant, please provide the name of the grantor and the grant name and number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about funding may reveal incentives or constraints and is particularly relevant for research datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation — other comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for additional motivation-related notes not covered by previous questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe what instances represent
rubrics_metrics.description: What do the instances that comprise the dataset represent (e.g., documents, photos, people, countries)? Are there multiple types of instances (e.g., movies, users, and ratings; people and interactions between them; nodes and edges)? Please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides dataset consumers necessary context about the basic unit(s) of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide instance counts
rubrics_metrics.description: How many instances are there in total (of each type, if appropriate)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential for understanding dataset scale and feasibility for particular methods or analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain sampling vs population coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the dataset contain all possible instances or is it a sample (not necessarily random) of instances from a larger set? If the dataset is a sample, then what is the larger set? Is the sample representative of the larger set (e.g., geographic coverage)? If so, please describe how this representativeness was validated/verified. If it is not representative of the larger set, please describe why not (e.g., to cover a more diverse range of instances, because instances were withheld or unavailable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope and representativeness; consumers can judge generalizability and bias risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe data per instance (raw or features)
rubrics_metrics.description: What data does each instance consist of? 'Raw' data (e.g., unprocessed text or images) or features? In either case, please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps consumers understand whether preprocessing has been applied and whether the dataset supports tasks requiring raw signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document labels or targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a label or target associated with each instance? If so, please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies supervised targets, their meaning and extraction procedures—critical for training/evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report missing information
rubrics_metrics.description: Is any information missing from individual instances? If so, please provide a description, explaining why this information is missing (e.g., because it was unavailable). This does not include intentionally removed information, but might include, e.g., redacted text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables consumers to understand gaps and how they might affect downstream tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit relationships between instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Are relationships between individual instances made explicit (e.g., users’ movie ratings, social network links)? If so, please describe how these relationships are made explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether relational or graph structure is present and how to exploit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended data splits
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there recommended data splits (e.g., training, development/validation, testing)? If so, please provide a description of these splits, explaining the rationale behind them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports reproducibility and fair comparisons by explaining intended partitioning and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe errors, noise, redundancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any errors, sources of noise, or redundancies in the dataset? If so, please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alerts consumers to quality issues and potential preprocessing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained vs external resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the dataset self-contained, or does it link to or otherwise rely on external resources (e.g., websites, tweets, other datasets)? If it links to or relies on external resources, a) are there guarantees that they will exist, and remain constant, over time; b) are there official archival versions of the complete dataset (i.e., including the external resources as they existed at the time the dataset was created); c) are there any restrictions (e.g., licenses, fees) associated with any of the external resources that might apply to a dataset consumer? Please provide descriptions of all external resources and any restrictions associated with them, as well as links or other access points, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for reproducibility; external dependencies can break or change and may impose legal or practical constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential data presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the dataset contain data that might be considered confidential (e.g., data that is protected by legal privilege or by doctor–patient confidentiality, data that includes the content of individuals’ non-public communications)? If so, please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags legal/ethical constraints and the need for special handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offensive or upsetting content
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the dataset contain data that, if viewed directly, might be offensive, insulting, threatening, or might otherwise cause anxiety? If so, please describe why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns users of potentially harmful content; useful for managing access and downstream use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpopulation identification (people-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the dataset identify any subpopulations (e.g., by age, gender)? If so, please describe how these subpopulations are identified and provide a description of their respective distributions within the dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps assess fairness and distributional representativeness; grouped under people-related questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifiability of individuals (people-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it possible to identify individuals (i.e., one or more natural persons), either directly or indirectly (i.e., in combination with other data) from the dataset? If so, please describe how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential privacy consideration; informs de-identification and access controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive attributes presence (people-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the dataset contain data that might be considered sensitive in any way (e.g., data that reveals race or ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions or union memberships, or locations; financial or health data; biometric or genetic data; forms of government identification, such as social security numbers; criminal history)? If so, please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies attributes that can cause harm or legal constraints; supports risk assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection method per instance
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the data associated with each instance acquired? Was the data directly observable (e.g., raw text, movie ratings), reported by subjects (e.g., survey responses), or indirectly inferred/derived from other data (e.g., part-of-speech tags, model-based guesses for age or language)? If the data was reported by subjects or indirectly inferred/derived from other data, was the data validated/verified? If so, please describe how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides provenance and reliability information about observations and labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection mechanisms and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: What mechanisms or procedures were used to collect the data (e.g., hardware apparatuses or sensors, manual human curation, software programs, software APIs)? How were these mechanisms or procedures validated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies collection pipeline and any validation steps to assess trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy (if sample)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dataset is a sample from a larger set, what was the sampling strategy (e.g., deterministic, probabilistic with specific sampling probabilities)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables assessment of selection bias and representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who collected the data and compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Who was involved in the data collection process (e.g., students, crowdworkers, contractors) and how were they compensated (e.g., how much were crowdworkers paid)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about labor, potential quality/ethical implications related to worker compensation and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection timeframe and creation timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Over what timeframe was the data collected? Does this timeframe match the creation timeframe of the data associated with the instances (e.g., recent crawl of old news articles)? If not, please describe the timeframe in which the data associated with the instances was created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-related properties affect relevance, concept drift, and temporal biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Were any ethical review processes conducted (e.g., by an institutional review board)? If so, please provide a description of these review processes, including the outcomes, as well as a link or other access point to any supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents oversight and approvals; helpful for compliance and risk evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of data for people-related datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you collect the data from the individuals in question directly, or obtain it via third parties or other sources (e.g., websites)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies indirect vs direct collection and implications for consent/notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of individuals (people-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Were the individuals in question notified about the data collection? If so, please describe (or show with screenshots or other information) how notice was provided, and provide a link or other access point to, or otherwise reproduce, the exact language of the notification itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents whether subjects were informed about collection and potential uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent from individuals (people-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the individuals in question consent to the collection and use of their data? If so, please describe (or show with screenshots or other information) how consent was requested and provided, and provide a link or other access point to, or otherwise reproduce, the exact language to which the individuals consented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for legal and ethical compliance; captures the scope of permitted uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism to revoke consent (people-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: If consent was obtained, were the consenting individuals provided with a mechanism to revoke their consent in the future or for certain uses? If so, please provide a description, as well as a link or other access point to the mechanism (if appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses ongoing privacy rights and maintenance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact analysis on data subjects (people-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has an analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects (e.g., a data protection impact analysis) been conducted? If so, please provide a description of this analysis, including the outcomes, as well as a link or other access point to any supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages proactive assessment of harms and mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing/cleaning/labeling performed
rubrics_metrics.description: Was any preprocessing/cleaning/labeling of the data done (e.g., discretization or bucketing, tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, SIFT feature extraction, removal of instances, processing of missing values)? If so, please provide a description. If not, you may skip the remaining questions in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes transformations that change the raw signal and affect downstream suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of raw data
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the 'raw' data saved in addition to the preprocessed/cleaned/labeled data (e.g., to support unanticipated future uses)? If so, please provide a link or other access point to the 'raw' data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserving raw data supports future analyses, reprocessing, and auditing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of preprocessing software
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the software that was used to preprocess/clean/label the data available? If so, please provide a link or other access point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing code supports reproducibility and enables reuse of the exact preprocessing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing — other comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for additional preprocessing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past uses of the dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the dataset been used for any tasks already? If so, please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents provenance of models and research built on the dataset and helps users find prior evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository of works using dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a repository that links to any or all papers or systems that use the dataset? If so, please provide a link or other access point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates discovery of prior work and reuse examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential other tasks for dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: What (other) tasks could the dataset be used for?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps consumers consider alternative uses and whether dataset assumptions hold for those tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition/collection impact on future uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there anything about the composition of the dataset or the way it was collected and preprocessed/cleaned/labeled that might impact future uses? For example, is there anything that a dataset consumer might need to know to avoid uses that could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups (e.g., stereotyping, quality of service issues) or other risks or harms (e.g., legal risks, financial harms)? If so, please provide a description. Is there anything a dataset consumer could do to mitigate these risks or harms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages explicit statement of limitations and mitigation strategies to prevent misuse or harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tasks for which dataset should not be used
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there tasks for which the dataset should not be used? If so, please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against inappropriate or harmful applications and clarifies dataset limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses — other comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional notes on intended or unintended uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party distribution plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the dataset be distributed to third parties outside of the entity (e.g., company, institution, organization) on behalf of which the dataset was created? If so, please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States whether dataset is public/internal and any constraints around sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution mechanism and DOI
rubrics_metrics.description: How will the dataset will be distributed (e.g., tarball on website, API, GitHub)? Does the dataset have a digital object identifier (DOI)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies access method and persistence identifiers to support citation and discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When will the dataset be distributed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates release schedule and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and terms of use
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the dataset be distributed under a copyright or other intellectual property (IP) license, and/or under applicable terms of use (ToU)? If so, please describe this license and/or ToU, and provide a link or other access point to, or otherwise reproduce, any relevant licensing terms or ToU, as well as any fees associated with these restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential legal information that constrains reuse, redistribution, and derivative works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party IP restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Have any third parties imposed IP-based or other restrictions on the data associated with the instances? If so, please describe these restrictions, and provide a link or other access point to, or otherwise reproduce, any relevant licensing terms, as well as any fees associated with these restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents external legal constraints that may affect consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export controls and regulatory restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do any export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply to the dataset or to individual instances? If so, please describe these restrictions, and provide a link or other access point to, or otherwise reproduce, any supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alerts consumers to jurisdictional/regulatory constraints on distribution or use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution — other comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for distribution-related notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset support/hosting/maintenance responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Who will be supporting/hosting/maintaining the dataset?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies custodians and signals reliability and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for dataset manager
rubrics_metrics.description: How can the owner/curator/manager of the dataset be contacted (e.g., email address)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a way for consumers to request clarification, report issues, or propose contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erratum presence and link
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an erratum? If so, please provide a link or other access point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents known issues and corrections to support reproducibility and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update policy and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the dataset be updated (e.g., to correct labeling errors, add new instances, delete instances)? If so, please describe how often, by whom, and how updates will be communicated to dataset consumers (e.g., mailing list, GitHub)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies maintenance cadence and how consumers learn about changes; important for versioning and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention limits for people-related data
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dataset relates to people, are there applicable limits on the retention of the data associated with the instances (e.g., were the individuals in question told that their data would be retained for a fixed period of time and then deleted)? If so, please describe these limits and explain how they will be enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses privacy retention commitments and enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for older versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Will older versions of the dataset continue to be supported/hosted/maintained? If so, please describe how. If not, please describe how its obsolescence will be communicated to dataset consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies backward-compatibility guarantees and archival practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism for contributions and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If others want to extend/augment/build on/contribute to the dataset, is there a mechanism for them to do so? If so, please provide a description. Will these contributions be validated/verified? If so, please describe how. If not, why not? Is there a process for communicating/distributing these contributions to dataset consumers? If so, please provide a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes community contribution workflow, quality control, and dissemination of extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance — other comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for maintenance-related notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prescriptive and context-dependent guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The provided set of questions are not intended to be prescriptive; datasheets will necessarily vary depending on factors such as the domain or existing organizational infrastructure and workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages adaptation of the datasheet questions to domain-specific needs and organizational contexts rather than strict one-size-fits-all compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual reflection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of creating a datasheet is not intended to be automated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages manual reflection by dataset creators to surface assumptions, risks, and contextual details that automated tools would miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer as many questions as possible
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend answering as many questions as possible rather than skipping the datasheet creation process entirely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that not all questions will apply or be answerable but emphasizes partial documentation is better than none.
